cross_platform_plan: Single keydown handler in main.ts (note main.ts:415 already intercepts Ctrl/Meta combos for terminals - extend it so these shortcuts work while xterm has focus only where intended). Map Ctrl->Cmd on macOS (Cmd+F, Cmd+R as macOS refresh alternative to F5, Cmd+Enter). Also add a native macOS app menu (Edit menu with Copy/Paste/Select All is required on macOS for Cmd+C/V to work in webviews; View > Refresh; Find).

name: Drop folders onto the window to start Claude
description: Dragging one or more folders from Explorer onto the window starts a new Claude session in each and pins the folder in the sidebar.
behavior_details: DragEnter accepts FileDrop with Copy effect. On drop, for each path that is a directory: Start-Claude(path, '', Get-StartAccount) using default open mode (settings.openIn) and active profile (or settings.account), then Add-Pin(path) (adds to settings.pinned). Files are ignored.
cross_platform_plan: Tauri 2 window drag-drop event (getCurrentWebview().onDragDropEvent, type 'drop' gives paths) with dragDropEnabled true; check is_dir in Rust. Works for Finder and Explorer. Show a drop overlay on 'over'.

name: Refresh on window activation
description: Coming back to the window refreshes the session lists if session files changed while away.
behavior_details: On form Activated: if Loaded and the watcher-collected Changed set is non-empty -> Refresh-All (incremental index update of changed .jsonl files). (Comment says 'at most every 5 seconds'; throttling lives in Refresh-All/other slice.)
cross_platform_plan: Rust notify watcher (FSEvents on macOS, ReadDirectoryChangesW on Windows) collecting changed paths; on window focus event (tauri WindowEvent::Focused(true)) or debounced push via event, refresh the index incrementally.

name: Startup / load sequence
description: The window builds its first screen before showing, then fades in; it either shows the profile picker or enters the last profile directly.
behavior_details: Form Load: Start-Warmup (pre-warm, other slice); create handles for toolbar, body, search, avatar, usage ring; layout. Picker decision: show picker if settings.showPicker is true, or lastProfile is empty, or lastProfile is a path (not 'all') that no longer exists; else lastProfile 'all' -> Enter-Profile(null) (all accounts), else Enter-Profile(lastProfile). Form Shown: fade window in (opacity starts at 0), set Loaded, Restore-BackgroundTerms (reopen embedded terminals that were running), start live-session timer, Update-Usage, prepare fade overlay, enable file watchers (enabled only after showing to keep startup fast). App runs as modal ShowDialog (process exits when closed).
data_sources: settings.json showPicker, lastProfile (path to a Claude config dir or 'all'); pinned, account, openIn, groups, ungroupedCollapsed, showUsage, notify (defaults at line 99)
cross_platform_plan: Tauri: create window with visible:false, render first screen, then window.show() with a CSS opacity fade (native window alpha fade not needed). Same picker rules reading settings.json from Rust (use the same file location per OS: %APPDATA% / ~/Library/Application Support, or keep a shared path for migration). Start notify watchers and live/usage polling after the first paint. Restore background terminals via pty.rs (dependency).

name: Open file / folder in VS Code from source control
description: Open file (hover icon or double-click) and 'Open folder in VS Code' from the commit menu.
behavior_details: Uses $CodeExe (LocalAppData\Programs\Microsoft VS Code\Code.exe, then Program Files, then 'code' on PATH), launched hidden with the quoted full path; only if the file exists.
cross_platform_plan: Rust command open_in_vscode(path): Windows - same lookup; macOS - `open -a "Visual Studio Code" <path>` or the `code` CLI at /usr/local/bin/code or /Applications/Visual Studio Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/bin/code. Fall back to opener's default app if VS Code is missing.

name: Theme palette and DPI scaling
description: All controls draw from one shared color palette (Bg, Side, Card, Alt, Ctrl, CtrlHover, Track, SegSel, Text, Muted, Border, Accent, AccentHover, Danger, Menu) that the host switches between light and dark mode. Every size is multiplied by a DPI scale factor.
behavior_details: Palette is set from the PowerShell side to match OS light/dark. Pal.S(v)=round(v*Scale). Dark detection elsewhere uses Bg brightness < 0.5 (DiffView). Fixed non-theme colors: traffic lights #FF5F57/#FEBC2E/#28C840, live green rgb(48,209,88), warning orange #FF9F0A, git lane colors #FFB000 #DC267F #40B0A6 #B66DFF #994F00, status colors M #E2C08D, A/U #73C991, D #F14C4C, R/C #4FC1FF, ! #E4676B, hunk blue #4FC1FF.
data_sources: None in this slice; values pushed from ClaudeManager.ps1 (theme detection lives there).
cross_platform_plan: Define CSS custom properties on :root for each palette token with a prefers-color-scheme: dark override (and a data-theme override if the app lets the user force a theme). Use CSS px (WebView handles DPI on both OSes), so Pal.S is unnecessary. Keep the fixed colors as constants.

name: Spring animation engine
description: Every motion in the app (hover fades, press darkening, gliding selection pills, toggles, scroll, popovers) uses a damped spring like SwiftUI, so things ease and slightly overshoot instead of linear tweens.
behavior_details: Spring(response s, damping fraction, epsilon): k=(2pi/response)^2, c=4pi*damping/response, semi-implicit Euler with 4 ms sub-steps, dt capped at 1/30 s; settles when |value-target|<eps and |vel|<eps*10, then snaps. One shared ~8 ms frame clock; Animator.After(ms, fn) schedules delayed callbacks on the same clock. Re-running a spring that is already animating just retargets it (keeps velocity). Specific tunings: hover 0.22/1.0, press 0.16/1.0, Segmented pill 0.34/0.8, Toggle knob 0.32/0.72, sidebar selection 0.3/0.82 (top) and 0.3/0.9 (height), list scroll 0.36/1.0, scrollbar fade 0.25, ProfilePopup 0.28/0.9, UsagePopup 0.18/0.95, SearchPopup 0.16/1.0, tab pill 0.3/0.86+0.3/0.9, window fade-in 0.32, screen crossfade 0.3, usage ring fill 0.6.
cross_platform_plan: Already partly ported in src/spring.ts (Spring, animate via requestAnimationFrame, smoothScroll). Keep the same response/damping numbers per control so feel matches. Add an 'after(ms)' helper or use setTimeout. Respect prefers-reduced-motion by snapping.

name: MacButton (push button)
description: Rounded button in four kinds: primary (accent fill, white text), secondary (control fill with border), danger (control fill, red text, border), plain (transparent until hovered). Optional icon glyph before the text, or icon-only.
behavior_details: Hover crossfades fill to hover color (spring); press darkens fill ~8%; radius 7px default; glyph+text centered as a group with 6px gap, glyph centered on its real ink bounds; FitWidth = text width + 26px padding (12px if icon-only). Hand cursor.
cross_platform_plan: A <button class='btn btn--primary|secondary|danger|plain'> with CSS transitions (or spring-driven custom properties) for hover/active. Use an icon font/SVG set that exists on both OSes (do not rely on Segoe MDL2/Fluent glyphs, which are missing on macOS) — bundle e.g. Lucide/Codicons SVGs.

name: Segmented control
description: macOS segmented picker; clicking a segment slides a raised white pill under it with a soft shadow.
behavior_details: Segment chosen by x position (equal widths). Pill glides with bouncy spring (0.34, 0.8). Text color fades from muted to full as the pill arrives. Thin dividers between segments are drawn only where the pill is not adjacent. Fires SelectedChanged; setting the index before display snaps without animation.
cross_platform_plan: Radio-group of buttons with an absolutely positioned pill element animated by spring.ts on translateX. Add arrow-key navigation (role=radiogroup) for accessibility.

name: Toggle switch
description: iOS/macOS on/off switch; the track fades from gray to accent and the white knob springs across with a slight bounce; the knob stretches wider while the mouse is pressed.
behavior_details: Click flips Checked and fires CheckedChanged. Knob spring 0.32/0.72; press stretch up to 5px. Same visual switch is drawn (non-animated) inside ProfilePopup toggle rows.
cross_platform_plan: <button role='switch' aria-checked> or styled checkbox with CSS; animate knob with spring.ts or a cubic-bezier overshoot; :active widens knob. Space/Enter toggles.

name: Profile avatar
description: Round profile picture with the profile's initial(s) on a colored circle (Chrome-profile style). Shows an accent ring on hover (or permanently when Ring is set), and squeezes slightly on press. Also rendered as small bitmaps for menu items.
behavior_details: Initial text centered on actual glyph ink bounds (not line box). Font size = 42% of diameter for one character, 30% for two or more. Ring = 2px accent stroke, alpha follows hover spring. Avatar.Render(initial, fill, ink, size) produces images used as menu icons (e.g. profile switcher entries).
data_sources: Profile name/color come from the host (profiles slice).
cross_platform_plan: A div with border-radius:50%, background color and centered text (flex + line-height:1; text-box-trim where supported) at the same size ratios; ring via box-shadow transition. Use it inline in menus instead of bitmaps. Font: system-ui semibold rather than 'Segoe UI Semibold'.

name: RoundPanel (cards, search field, input boxes)
description: Rounded container with fill and border; can fade in a hover fill and an accent focus ring (used for the search field and the text box in prompts).
behavior_details: SetHighlight(on) springs (0.25) between normal and highlight stroke/fill. Prompt dialog uses it so the input border turns accent on focus.
cross_platform_plan: CSS: border-radius, border, transition on border-color/background; :focus-within for the focus ring.

name: Traffic-light window buttons
description: Red/yellow/green close, minimize, zoom circles at the top left. When hovered, x / - / + symbols appear inside; when the window is inactive they turn gray and only regain color on hover.
behavior_details: 12px circles, 8px gap, faint dark outline. Click zone is the circle column only (clicks in the gap are ignored). Close -> CloseClick, yellow -> MinClick, green -> ZoomClick (ToggleZoom maximizes to the monitor's work area / restores). Symbol alpha follows hover spring. SetActive(false) when the window loses focus.
cross_platform_plan: macOS: use native traffic lights (tauri.conf titleBarStyle 'Overlay' + hiddenTitle, trafficLightPosition) and drop the custom ones; reserve left padding for them. Windows: either keep custom-drawn traffic lights in HTML (frameless window, decorations:false) calling appWindow.close()/minimize()/toggleMaximize(), with window focus/blur events to gray them, or use native caption buttons on the right. Pick one per OS via navigator/platform check.

name: Borderless main window (MacForm)
description: Frameless window with system drop shadow, 1px border when not maximized, drag-to-move from the custom title bar, resize from any edge/corner (6px grab zone), and zoom that maximizes to the monitor working area (not covering the taskbar). Still minimizable from the taskbar.
behavior_details: Edge hit-testing only in Normal state. DragMove starts a native window move. ToggleZoom toggles Maximized/Normal. Border drawn only when not maximized.
cross_platform_plan: Tauri: decorations:false (Windows) with data-tauri-drag-region on the title bar and Tauri's built-in resize borders (Windows 'shadow: true'); double-click title bar to maximize. macOS: keep native decorations with titleBarStyle:'Overlay' so resizing, shadow, fullscreen and Mission Control work natively. appWindow.toggleMaximize() for zoom.

name: Window fade-in on first show
description: New windows fade in from transparent to opaque instead of popping.
behavior_details: Spring 0.32 on opacity 0->1, then opacity forced to exactly 1.
cross_platform_plan: Create window with visible:false, show after first paint, and fade the body via CSS opacity transition (window-level opacity is not portable). Optional.

name: Screen crossfade overlay
description: When switching between major views, a snapshot of the old screen is laid on top and fades out over the new content so the change is a smooth crossfade with no flash.
behavior_details: Click-through, non-activating overlay reused across transitions; buffer pre-warmed for the window size; a new transition cancels a running fade. Fade spring 0.3.
cross_platform_plan: Not needed as a screenshot trick: in the webview crossfade the two view containers with CSS opacity (or View Transitions API in WebView2; WKWebView supports it on Safari 18+, fall back to opacity). Drop the Win32 layered-window code.

name: MacList: smooth scrolling with rubber-band edges and overlay scrollbar
description: All lists (sidebar tree, sessions table, history) scroll with spring smoothing; scrolling past the top/bottom stretches with Apple-style resistance then springs back. A thin rounded scrollbar thumb appears while scrolling and fades away about 1 s after the last scroll. The thumb can be dragged.
behavior_details: Wheel step = 36px*2.4 per notch. Overscroll allowed up to 2*half view height in raw input, mapped through rubber curve (1-1/(x*0.55/d+1))*d. 140 ms after the last wheel event, an out-of-range target snaps back to the edge. Thumb: 6px wide, 10px from right, min height 32px, shrinks (min 12px) while rubber-banding. Show on scroll; hide check after 1100 ms if no wheel for 1000 ms and not dragging. Thumb drag starts if click is within 4px left of thumb while it is visible (>10% opacity). Resize clamps scroll instantly. Content keeps scroll position on SetRows.
cross_platform_plan: macOS already has native rubber-band and overlay scrollbars in WKWebView — use native overflow scrolling there. On Windows WebView2, use overflow:auto with thin custom scrollbar CSS (::-webkit-scrollbar, auto-hide via a class toggled on scroll with 1 s timeout) and optional spring.ts smoothScroll for wheel; skip rubber-band on Windows or emulate via transform. Do not fight trackpad momentum on macOS.

name: MacList: selection model and keyboard navigation
description: Click selects a row; Ctrl+click toggles, Shift+click selects a range (multi-select lists); Ctrl+A selects all; arrow keys, Home, End, PageUp, PageDown move the selection skipping non-selectable rows (section headings, hints); Enter or double-click opens/activates the row. Right-click on an unselected row selects only it; right-click on an already selected row keeps the multi-selection for the context menu.
behavior_details: Only Kind folder/group rows are selectable. Shift+arrows extends from the anchor. Page size = visible rows - 1. Selection is preserved by row Key across refreshes (SetRows); focus row = first selected. Double-click on a project's chevron area (x<24px) does not activate. Selection is accent-filled; in the sidebar it is dimmed (accent mixed 35% with control color) when the list does not have focus. SelectionChanged fires only when the selection actually changes. EnsureVisible scrolls the newly focused row into view with the spring. Focus is taken on mouse down.
cross_platform_plan: Implement in TS on a virtualized list: keep a Set of selected keys, anchor and focus index; map Ctrl to Cmd on macOS (metaKey) for toggle and select-all; keep Shift for range. Use aria-selected/role=listbox|tree. Preserve selection by key when re-rendering after each data refresh.

name: MacList: gliding sidebar selection pill
description: In the sidebar the accent selection highlight slides (with a little bounce) from the old row to the new one and resizes to the new row's height; text turns white only once the pill has arrived.
behavior_details: Springs: top 0.3/0.82, height 0.3/0.9. Row draws 'on' style only when pill is within half a row height of it. Snaps (no animation) when the list is hidden or first shown.
cross_platform_plan: One absolutely positioned highlight element inside the scroll container animated by spring.ts (translateY + height); rows get a .on class when the spring is within half a row.

name: MacList: hover fade
description: Hovered rows get a soft rounded highlight that fades in; not shown on selected rows, section headings or hint rows.
behavior_details: Hover spring 0.18; table rows use 70% intensity, sidebar full. Inset 4px (sidebar) / 6px (table), radius 6px.
cross_platform_plan: CSS :hover background with transition 150ms.

name: Sidebar tree rows: projects, folders, sections, hints, 'Show more'
description: The sidebar shows a PROJECTS section with each user-defined project (group) row having a disclosure arrow, a project icon, the name in bold, and a count badge of its sessions; nested folder rows under it show folder icon (star if pinned, warning icon if the folder no longer exists, dimmed), name, and a relative time on the right ('5h ago'). Then a FOLDERS · N section with every folder not in a project. Hint rows ('Drag folders here', 'No projects yet. Click + to create one.', 'No matching projects') appear in gray. Long projects show 5 folders and a 'Show N more' accent link; expanded ones show 'Show less'.
behavior_details: Section heading rows are 30px, group 34px, folder 32px, more/hint 28px. Clicking a section heading toggles it (chevron shows only on hover, at right). Clicking the arrow column (x<24px) of a project toggles collapse; arrow glyph switches right/down. 'Show more' threshold: more than 6 folders -> show first 5 + 'Show N more'; when expanded and >6 shows 'Show less'. While searching all groups open and all folders shown. Nesting guide: thin vertical line at indent, ending half way on the last child. Indent step 22px. Badge = pill min 22px wide, 18px tall, number centered; white-translucent on selected rows. Detail time uses Ago(): 'just now', 'Nm ago', 'Nh ago', 'Yesterday', 'Nd ago', 'MMM d', 'MMM d, yyyy' (other year), 'no sessions'. Folder rows without sessions show no detail. Search matches group name, folder name, or any session full title (excluding '(no prompt)'). Row keys: 'g:<name>', 'f:<path lower>', 'm:<name>', 's:projects', 's:folders'.
data_sources: Project names, member folders, collapsed[] / showAll[] / foldersCollapsed come from the host's settings.json (ClaudeManager.ps1 slice — keys owned there). Sessions from ~/.claude*/projects/*.jsonl.
cross_platform_plan: Render the same row model in TS (port Tree.Build logic to Rust or TS). Paths: trim trailing '\' and also '/' on macOS; compare case-insensitively on Windows and macOS (APFS default) but use Path::file_name for display. Persist collapse/showAll state in the same settings.json keys as the PS app for migration.

name: Live session dots
description: Rows for sessions/folders with a running Claude show a dot: green = open/idle, accent with a breathing halo = Claude is working. On selected rows the dot is white. In the table, a live session replaces its icon with the dot.
behavior_details: Dot 8px. Working halo grows up to +7px and fades, cycle 1.4 s (cosine). Only the dot regions repaint every 40 ms, and the timer runs only while a working dot is on screen. Live level: 1 open, 2 busy. Also shown in search results.
data_sources: Live state from LiveScan (<profile>/sessions/<pid>.json with status 'busy', or <pid>.<hash>.key + process command line) — data-service slice.
cross_platform_plan: CSS: .live-dot green; .live-dot.busy accent with a ::after pulse keyframe animation (1.4 s ease-in-out infinite). Pure CSS, no timers. Live detection backend: Rust sysinfo crate for pid alive + process name + cmdline (works on Windows and macOS); allow process names claude/node and macOS shells (zsh, bash, login, Terminal/iTerm are not parents necessarily).

name: Drag folders into projects (drag-reorder)
description: Folder rows can be dragged; after moving 6px a floating accent pill with the folder name follows the cursor; a valid target (a project row or the FOLDERS heading) gets an accent tint and outline; releasing drops the folder there (add to project / remove from project). Dragging near the top or bottom edge auto-scrolls.
behavior_details: Only rows with Draggable (folders) can be dragged; only rows with AcceptsDrop (group rows, the FOLDERS section) are targets; cannot drop onto itself. Auto-scroll 12px per mouse move when within 28px of top/bottom. Drag pill is hidden if narrower than 30px (near right edge). Drop fires RowDropped(source,target); what it does (move between projects, unassign) is in the host slice.
data_sources: Host updates project membership in settings.json.
cross_platform_plan: Pointer-events based drag in TS (pointerdown/move/up with 6px threshold, setPointerCapture) rather than HTML5 DnD so the custom pill and auto-scroll match on both WebView2 and WKWebView. Also accept OS file/folder drops (Tauri onDragDropEvent) onto a project as a bonus.

name: Table list (sessions / history) with columns, zebra, merged selection, tags and commit graph
description: Table mode of the list: optional column header with muted titles and bottom border, one stretch column taking leftover width (min 120px), optional zebra striping, adjacent selected rows merged into one rounded selection block, icon column, secondary columns in muted color, ellipsis truncation. History rows show a commit graph and branch/tag pills.
behavior_details: Branch/tag pills sit at the right end of the first column (max 120px each, 18px tall); a tag starting with '*' is the current HEAD and is accent-tinted; pills are dropped when less than 70px would remain for text. Rows can have custom heights. Header stays fixed while scrolling.
data_sources: Session rows from transcripts; history from git log (source control slice).
cross_platform_plan: CSS grid rows inside a virtualized scroller (sessions can number thousands); sticky header; :nth-child zebra; merged selection via adjacent-sibling border-radius rules. Pills as spans.

name: Commit graph lanes
description: History list shows a VS Code-style commit graph: colored lanes, curved connectors for branches and merges, filled dot for a normal commit, hollow ring for merges, ring with dot for HEAD (larger).
behavior_details: Layout walks commits newest-first; each lane waits for a parent hash; first parent continues the lane, other parents branch to free lanes with new colors; trailing empty lanes are trimmed; MaxLanes sets the graph width. Lane x = 16 + lane*14 + 6 px. Curves are cubic beziers between lanes. 5 rotating colors. Dot radius 4px (HEAD 5.5px) with a background-colored halo.
data_sources: git log --format with hashes and parent hashes (source control slice).
cross_platform_plan: Port GitGraph.Layout to Rust or TS unchanged; draw each row as an inline SVG (paths + circles) in the first cell. Platform neutral.

name: Console embedding and focus (TermHost)
description: Each terminal tab hosts a real Windows console window running Claude inside the app; clicking the console gives it keyboard focus; only one console's input is linked at a time.
behavior_details: Embeds by reparenting a ConsoleWindowClass window and stripping its frame; unembed either hidden (keeps running in background) or back to desktop at a position (pop out). Focus via AttachThreadInput to the console's real UI thread found by enumerating conhost threads. WM_PARENTNOTIFY left/right/middle click triggers focus. FindChild uses a ToolHelp snapshot to find a child process by exe name.
cross_platform_plan: Drop entirely. The Tauri app already uses portable-pty + xterm.js (ConPTY on Windows, openpty on macOS), so focus is just xterm.focus() on click/tab switch. 'Pop out' becomes opening a new Tauri WebviewWindow attached to the same PTY session id (dependency: terminals slice / pty.rs).

name: Terminal tab strip
description: Safari/Chrome-style tab bar: a pinned home tab (house icon + 'Home'/'Sessions' title) on the left, a divider, then one tab per open terminal with a terminal icon, bold title, and a muted subtitle (e.g. folder/profile). The active tab has a raised pill that glides between tabs. Active or hovered tabs show a pop-out button and a close (x) button. Thin dividers between inactive neighbours. Tabs share the width and shrink; extra tabs go into an overflow 'more' button showing a chevron and the hidden count.
behavior_details: Tab width between 150 (min to fit) and 250px, never below 110px; overflow button 52px. The active tab is always visible: if it would be hidden it replaces the last visible slot. Left click selects; middle click or x closes ('Close terminal'); pop-out button 'Pop out to its own window'; right-click opens that tab's context menu (TabMenu, contents in host slice); clicking Home selects the main view. Tooltips: title + newline + subtitle; 'All open terminals' on the more button. More button opens a menu headed 'N open terminal(s)' (disabled label) listing every tab with terminal icon, checkmark on the active one, and its subtitle right-aligned like a shortcut. Pill springs 0.3/0.86 (x) and 0.3/0.9 (width); snaps on resize. Rename(tag,title) updates a tab title live.
data_sources: Open terminal list from the host.
cross_platform_plan: HTML flex tab bar with a spring-animated pill element; ResizeObserver recomputes how many fit; overflow menu as a custom popover menu. Add keyboard shortcuts expected on both OSes: Ctrl/Cmd+W close, Ctrl+Tab / Cmd+Shift+] next, Cmd/Ctrl+1..9 select (new, not in original). Middle-click via auxclick. Tab bar sits in the title bar drag region (exclude buttons from data-tauri-drag-region).

name: Profile popover menu
description: Chrome-style profile menu that drops down under the avatar at the top-right: large header with a 64px avatar, the current profile name and email; a gray label row (e.g. 'Other profiles'); rows for other profiles with 32px avatar, name and email; action rows with icon + text (e.g. add profile, manage); toggle rows with icon, text and an on/off switch; separators.
behavior_details: Width 300px, rounded 12px, drop shadow, border. Right-aligned to the anchor's right edge, 6px below; appears with fade + 8px slide-down (spring 0.28/0.9) and reverses on close. Closes on Esc, on losing focus (click outside), or after picking a profile/action. Clicking a toggle flips it in place and fires Picked without closing. Hover highlights only clickable rows with hand cursor. Picked(id) handlers are in the host slice.
data_sources: Profile list and settings from host (profiles slice).
cross_platform_plan: An in-window HTML popover (absolutely positioned div with backdrop click and Esc to close, focus trap) — simpler and consistent on both OSes than a separate OS window. Animate opacity/translateY with spring.ts.

name: macOS-style context and dropdown menus
description: All right-click and dropdown menus look like macOS menus: one icon column (icon or checkmark in accent), text after it, keyboard shortcut right-aligned in gray, chevron for submenus, separators aligned with text, red text and red highlight for destructive items, rounded accent highlight for the hovered item, disabled items used as smaller gray section labels, profile avatars as item icons. Every item in a menu has the same width (min 160px, max 520px).
behavior_details: Items are padded to fit shortcut + arrow; item height = text height + 12px; separator 9px; submenus styled automatically when opened. Selected item text is white; shortcut text 86% white on highlight. Disabled items without icon render at 92% font size as section labels.
data_sources: Menu contents built in the host slice.
cross_platform_plan: Build one reusable TS ContextMenu component (HTML popover positioned at cursor, clamped to the window, keyboard navigation with arrows/Enter/Esc, submenus on hover/right arrow, typeahead optional) with item props {icon, label, shortcut, checked, danger, disabled, submenu}. Show shortcuts as Ctrl+X on Windows and ⌘X on macOS. Alternative: Tauri native Menu API for context menus (native look per OS) — but native menus cannot show avatar images easily; the custom HTML menu gives parity. Also provide a native macOS app menu bar (App/Edit/Window) so Cmd+Q/Cmd+C/Cmd+V work.

name: Themed tooltips
description: Tooltips use the app's menu color, border and font instead of OS-yellow/white ones.
behavior_details: Show after 450 ms, reshow 80 ms, auto-hide after 12 s; padding 9x5px; multi-line allowed.
cross_platform_plan: Small custom tooltip component (data-tip attribute + delegated mouseenter with 450 ms delay) styled with palette tokens; native title attribute is inconsistent between WebView2 and WKWebView.

name: Usage ring in the title bar
description: Small circular progress ring in the title bar showing the current-session plan usage (highest 'Current session' % across shown profiles); green/accent under 70%, orange 70-89%, red 90%+. While loading it shows a spinning accent arc; if all fetches failed it shows a gray ring with a short red arc at the top. Hovering opens the usage popover immediately; it closes once the mouse is over neither ring nor popover; clicking also opens it.
behavior_details: Fill animates with spring 0.6. Spinner rotates 9 degrees every 30 ms while state=loading. State: 0 loading (no plans yet), 1 ok (any profile has limits), 2 failed. Falls back to local 5-hour-window fraction (current block tokens / peak block in last 8 days) when no plan percent is known. Hover watcher polls every 120 ms. Track color brightens on hover.
cross_platform_plan: SVG circle with stroke-dasharray animated by spring.ts; CSS rotate animation for loading. Popover open on mouseenter, close via mouseleave of a shared wrapper (ring + popover) with a short grace delay instead of polling.

name: Usage popover panel
description: Hover card showing 'USAGE' header with the scope (profile name or 'All profiles') and plan name ('· Max plan'), a spinner while refreshing, a status line ('Loading your plan limits...', 'Plan limits not loaded yet', 'Checking...', 'No plan limits available', 'Updated 12s ago · refreshing...', 'Numbers from 5m ago · usage service busy, will check again shortly'); then for each profile (name shown in bold when more than one) each limit: label ('Current session', 'Weekly · all models', 'Weekly · <model>'), 'N% used' colored by level, a progress bar, and reset text ('Resets in 2h 14m · 3:00 PM', 'Resets tomorrow 9:00 AM', 'Resets Mon 9:00 AM', 'Resets now'). Errors show as a gray line ('Not signed in', 'Sign-in expired — use this profile once to refresh', 'Usage service busy', 'Usage service unavailable (code)', 'Could not reach Anthropic (offline?)', 'Could not read usage'). Footer: 'This PC · today 1.2M · week 8.4M' with a 7-bar mini chart (today highlighted in accent). Breathing skeleton bars while nothing has loaded.
behavior_details: Width 330px, height fits content and resizes when content changes; does not take focus; fade+slide in (spring 0.18/0.95, starts at 55% opacity so it's visible on first frame). While open: repaint every 1 s (countdowns), local token recount every 30 s. On open, plan limits are refreshed only if older than 5 minutes (comment mentions 10 s but code uses 300 s staleness). 'Ago' format: 'just now' <5 s, 'Ns ago', 'Nm ago', else time. Until(): '<1 min' -> 'less than a minute', '>=1h' -> 'Hh Mm', else 'Mm SSs'. Reset text uses relative only when <24 h. Token formatting: K/M with one decimal below 100K/10M. Panel clock repaint every 30 s even when closed.
data_sources: Plan cache file (Plan.CachePath, set by host, JSON array [{profile, plan, fetched, limits:[{label, percent, resets}]}] — no tokens stored); profile .credentials.json; local transcripts.
cross_platform_plan: HTML popover component fed by Tauri commands get_usage_local(roots) and get_plan_limits(profiles) implemented in Rust (background threads/tokio). Store cache in app data dir (Windows %APPDATA%\ClaudeManager, macOS ~/Library/Application Support/ClaudeManager) with the same JSON shape. Use Intl.DateTimeFormat for times so 12/24h follows the OS.

name: Plan limits fetch (Anthropic OAuth usage API)
description: Reads each profile's sign-in token locally and asks Anthropic's usage endpoint for the same numbers as Claude Code's /usage. Shows last good numbers if the service is temporarily busy.
behavior_details: GET https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage with Authorization Bearer <claudeAiOauth.accessToken>, header anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20, User-Agent claude-manager, 15 s timeout. Skips call if token expiresAt (ms) is past -> 'Sign-in expired'. Per-credential memo: reuse a successful result for 5 min. On HTTP 429: global back-off for max(600, min(3600, Retry-After or 120)) s. 401 -> sign-in expired. Parses 'limits' array (group session/weekly, kind, scope.model.display_name, percent, resets_at); fallback to legacy five_hour/seven_day {utilization, resets_at}. Plan name from claudeAiOauth.subscriptionType, capitalized. Merge rule: transient errors (not sign-in related) keep the old numbers marked stale. Retry logic: keep retrying expired/busy; skip only when all profiles have limits or are 'Not signed in' and data <5 min old. Shows cached numbers immediately on start or profile change.
data_sources: <profile dir>/.credentials.json (claudeAiOauth.accessToken, expiresAt, subscriptionType); plan cache JSON.
cross_platform_plan: Rust reqwest call in the backend (never expose token to the webview). macOS caveat: Claude Code on macOS stores OAuth credentials in the login Keychain (service 'Claude Code-credentials'), not a .credentials.json — read via security-framework crate (or `security find-generic-password -s 'Claude Code-credentials' -w`), falling back to the file; for extra profiles with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR check how the keychain entry is named. Keep the same throttling and error strings.

name: Local token usage counting
description: Counts tokens from Claude Code transcripts on this computer for today, the last 7 days (per-day bars), and the current 5-hour window, without sending anything anywhere.
behavior_details: Scans *.jsonl recursively (includes sub-agent transcripts) under each profile's projects folder, files modified in last 8 days. Counts assistant lines with message.usage, skipping model '<synthetic>'; tokens = input + output + cache_creation_input (cache reads excluded). De-duplicates by message.id (one reply logged per content block). 5-hour windows start at the hour of the first reply and end after 5 h or after a 5 h gap; PeakBlock = biggest window; current window active if now < start+5h. Per-file cache keyed by last write time. Runs at below-normal thread priority.
cross_platform_plan: Port to Rust (walkdir + serde_json, rayon) as a Tauri command; cache by (path, mtime). Profile roots: ~/.claude and the app's extra profile dirs on both OSes.

name: Split button (primary action with dropdown)
description: One rounded accent button with a main part (icon + label, e.g. 'Commit') and a separate arrow part on the right (30px) divided by a thin line; hover lightens only the part under the mouse; disabled state is faded.
behavior_details: Left click on main part -> MainClick; on arrow -> ArrowClick (host shows a menu of alternate actions). Ignores clicks when disabled or non-left button.
cross_platform_plan: Two adjacent <button>s in a rounded group with CSS hover per part; arrow opens the shared ContextMenu component anchored below.

name: Text tabs with gliding underline
description: Plain text tabs (e.g. 'Changes 3 | History') where the selected one is full color and an accent underline glides to it.
behavior_details: Items spaced 18px; underline 2px with springs 0.3/0.86 and 0.3/0.9; SetItems (e.g. count change) re-snaps underline without animation; click selects and fires SelectedChanged.
cross_platform_plan: Buttons in a row + absolutely positioned underline animated with spring.ts; role=tablist.

name: Source control change list
description: VS Code-style list with 'STAGED CHANGES' and 'CHANGES' section headers (count pill on the right), file rows showing name colored by status, the folder path in muted text after it, and the status letter (M, A, U, D, R, C, !) at the right edge. Hovering a row reveals icon buttons: file rows in Changes: Open file, Discard changes, Stage; in Staged: Open file, Unstage; section headers: Changes -> Discard all changes, Stage all; Staged -> Unstage all. Empty state 'No changes'.
behavior_details: Section rows 30px, files 26px. Deleted files show name muted. Click selects a file (fires SelectionChanged -> diff shown); double-click (not on a button) opens it (ItemOpened); Up/Down move selection between files and scroll into view; wheel scroll 3 rows/notch with spring. Selection kept across refresh by path+section. Tooltip shows the action name over buttons, otherwise the full file path. Selected row is accent when focused, gray when not. Actions emitted as ItemAction(item, action) with ids open/discard/stage/unstage/stageAll/discardAll/unstageAll — git commands live in host slice (discard should confirm via Dlg).
data_sources: git status (host); git runs with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and LANG=en_US.UTF-8, UTF-8 output, in background.
cross_platform_plan: HTML list with hover-revealed icon buttons; Rust command runs git via std::process::Command (set CREATE_NO_WINDOW on Windows so no console flashes; same env vars). Locate git on macOS PATH (GUI apps get a minimal PATH: add /usr/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin, /usr/local/bin or read the login shell PATH).

name: Diff viewer
description: Unified diff view with old/new line number gutter, green background for added lines, red for removed, light-blue hunk headers (@@ ...), gray file header bars with the file path (new files show 'path  (new file)' as all-added lines), muted meta lines ('\ No newline at end of file', 'Binary file not shown'). Smooth vertical scrolling and Shift+wheel horizontal scrolling with the gutter staying fixed. Ctrl+C copies the whole diff as text with +/-/space prefixes. Empty text 'Select a file to see its changes' or a caller message.
behavior_details: Header noise (index, ---, +++, new file, deleted file, similarity, rename, old/new mode) hidden. Line numbers parsed from @@ -a,b +c,d. Tabs shown as 4 spaces. Caps: 40,000 diff lines, 20,000 lines for new files. Trailing blank meta lines trimmed; empty diff -> empty message. Vertical wheel = 3 lines/notch; horizontal 60px/notch, both spring 0.3. Different add/delete tints for light and dark themes. Gutter 96px.
data_sources: git diff output / file contents from host.
cross_platform_plan: Port the parser to TS; render with a virtualized list of monospace rows (position:sticky gutter, horizontal overflow). Native text selection is a bonus; keep Ctrl/Cmd+C copy-all when nothing is selected. Monospace font stack: 'Cascadia Mono', Consolas (Win) / 'SF Mono', Menlo (mac).

name: Confirm / message dialogs (Ask, Dlg.Show)
description: Themed modal dialog replacing OS message boxes: bold title (first line of the message), muted explanation (rest of the text, collapsed blank lines), and right-aligned buttons. Confirm dialogs show 'Cancel' plus a confirm button named after the action (the caption, e.g. 'Delete', 'Discard', 'Undo commit'; caption 'Commit' -> 'Stage all & commit'; 'Close terminal' -> 'Close'; empty or 'Claude Manager' -> 'OK'). Warning confirmations use a red danger button. Info messages show a single 'OK'.
behavior_details: Width 440px, 22px padding, buttons min 96px, 32px tall, 8px apart, primary button bold, rounded 12px with shadow and border, centered on the parent window, modal. Enter = primary, Esc or close = cancel. Returns 'Yes'/'No' or 'OK'/'Cancel' to mimic MessageBox.
cross_platform_plan: In-window HTML modal (<dialog> element with backdrop) returning a Promise<string>; same title/body split and button naming rules. Button order: keep Cancel left of confirm (matches macOS; also fine on Windows). Do not use OS dialogs (Tauri dialog plugin) to keep the look consistent, except optionally on macOS for destructive confirms.

name: Text input prompt (Prompt, Dlg.Input)
description: Themed one-line input dialog (used for naming/renaming projects, sessions, etc.): bold title, muted prompt text, a rounded text field prefilled with the current value and fully selected, Cancel and OK buttons.
behavior_details: Field border turns accent when focused. Enter = OK (returns text), Esc/Cancel returns null -> Dlg.Input returns '' (like InputBox). Width 440px, centered on parent.
cross_platform_plan: Same <dialog> modal with an <input>, autofocus + select() on open; Promise<string|null>. Trim/validation is caller's responsibility (host slice).

name: Quick-open search results popover
description: Spotlight/quick-open style dropdown under the search field showing results grouped under section headings: projects (group), folders, and sessions. Each row has an icon (or live dot for running sessions), a bold title with muted subtitle after it (sessions show title on one line and subtitle below), and muted right-aligned text (e.g. time). The first pickable result is pre-selected in accent. An 'empty' row shows a centered message when nothing matches. A footer explains keys: '↑↓ move   ↵ open   esc close'.
behavior_details: Width = max(search field width, 460px), centered under the field, 6px gap; rounded 12px, shadow, border; never steals focus from the text box (typing continues). Fades in from 60% (spring 0.16). Row heights: section 26px, group/folder 34px, session 44px, empty 44px; footer 30px. Up/Down (driven from the text box by host) wrap around and skip non-pickable rows; Enter picks; mouse hover moves the selection; click picks. Esc/closing handled in host.

Keyboard handled on the input (ArrowUp/Down, Enter, Escape). Add Cmd+K / Ctrl+K (or Cmd/Ctrl+F) to focus search — check host slice for the existing shortcut.

name: Session transcript indexing (title, count, folder)
description: Each Claude Code transcript becomes a session entry with a label: the custom title if the user renamed it, else Claude's summary, else the first real user prompt, else '(no prompt)'. Also shows the number of user messages, size and last-modified time; the folder it belongs to is taken from the first 'cwd' in the file.
behavior_details: Whitespace collapsed; label truncated to 140 chars + '...', full text to 600 chars. User message count excludes tool_result lines; first prompt skips isMeta lines and text starting with '<' (command/system tags). custom-title lines: last one wins; summary: first one wins. Incremental parsing: remembers byte offset of last complete line and reads only new data; restarts if file shrank; a trailing partial line is counted but re-read later. Cache by path+mtime; warm-up runs in parallel at below-normal priority. Sessions with 0 user messages are excluded from the index. Session id = file name; Slug = parent dir name (used as project path when cwd missing). File opened with full sharing so Claude can keep writing.
cross_platform_plan: Already started in src-tauri/src/sessions.rs — make sure it matches these rules (custom-title, summary, isMeta, '<' filter, tool_result exclusion, 140/600 truncation, incremental offset cache, zero-count exclusion). Use rayon for warm-up.

name: Project grouping and pinned folders
description: Sessions are grouped into folders by working directory; pinned folders appear even with no sessions and sort first (star icon); folders that no longer exist are flagged missing (dimmed, warning icon). Folders sort by most recent session. Sessions inside sort newest first. Can filter by active profile.
behavior_details: Grouping key: cwd with trailing backslash trimmed, case-insensitive, else slug. Profile filter compares SessionInfo.Account case-insensitively; empty = all profiles. CountFor gives the session count per profile (for profile menus). Older flat Rows() view: subtitle 'N session(s)   ·   <ago>' with search over path and labels.
data_sources: Pinned list from settings.json (host slice key).
cross_platform_plan: Port to Rust/TS; normalize both '\' and '/' trailing separators; existence check via std::path::Path::is_dir.

name: Live session detection
description: Detects which Claude Code sessions are currently running and whether they are busy, to drive the green/pulsing dots.
behavior_details: Reads <profile>/sessions/<pid>.json {pid, sessionId, status, cwd}; alive check via process; PID-reuse guard (process name must be claude/node/pwsh/powershell/cmd/bash/wt/windowsterminal/conhost/openconsole, else ignored but file kept); dead pid -> file deleted. status 'busy' -> level 2. Newer Claude writes <pid>.<hash>.key: session id from command line (--resume/-r/--session-id <uuid>) else newest jsonl written since process start (minus 5 s) not already claimed, processed in process-start order; busy if jsonl modified in last 8 s; cwd = last 'cwd' in final 256 KB of the transcript. Command line cache per pid (cleared over 500).
cross_platform_plan: Rust with sysinfo crate (process exists, name, cmd, start_time) — works on Windows and macOS. Extend the allowed-name list for macOS (claude, node, zsh, bash, sh, fish, login). Deleting stale files is fine on both.

name: Background git runner
description: Runs git commands off the UI thread and returns exit code, stdout and stderr; tagged variant lets late answers be ignored if the user already moved to another folder.
behavior_details: No console window, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 (never hangs on password prompts), LANG=en_US.UTF-8, UTF-8 decoding, optional stdin input (e.g. commit message).
cross_platform_plan: Tauri async command spawning git (tokio::process) with the same env; Windows creation_flags(CREATE_NO_WINDOW); macOS resolve PATH from login shell. Frontend keeps a request token per folder to drop stale results.

name: Session transcript parsing (Sessions.Read / ParseLine)
description: Every Claude Code transcript <profile>/projects/<slug>/<id>.jsonl becomes one session row with a title, message count, folder (cwd), time and size. Sessions with zero user messages are hidden.
behavior_details: SessionInfo fields: Id = file name without .jsonl; File = full path; Cwd; Label; Full; Count; Time = file LastWriteTime (local); SizeKB = ceil(len/1024); Account = profile dir; Slug = parent dir name. Per line (strip leading UTF-8 BOM U+FEFF, TrimEnd '\r'): user = line contains literal `"type":"user"` AND does NOT contain `"tool_result"` -> Count++. Cwd = first line containing `"cwd":"` -> JSON-parse and take top-level string `cwd`. Prompt = first user line that does not contain `"isMeta":true`; JSON-parse, message.content: if string use it; if array take first part with type=="text" and string `text`; skip if empty or TrimStart starts with '<' (command/system tags). Title: any line starting with `{"type":"custom-title"` -> `customTitle` (LAST one wins). Summary: first line starting with `{"type":"summary"` -> `summary`. Display: full = title ?? summary ?? prompt ?? "(no prompt)"; collapse all whitespace runs to one space and trim; Label = first 140 chars + "..." if longer; Full truncated to 600 chars + "...". All JSON errors are swallowed per line.
data_sources: Reads <profile>/projects/*/*.jsonl (depth 1 below projects; the PS lists -Recurse -Depth 1, i.e. subagent transcripts in deeper folders are NOT sessions). Opened with share read/write/delete so Claude can keep writing.
cross_platform_plan: Already partly in tauri/src-tauri/src/sessions.rs (read_session/parse_line/prompt_text). Verify exact parity: last custom-title wins, first summary, BOM strip, isMeta skip, '<' skip, 140/600 truncation, whitespace collapse, Count>0 filter, SizeKB ceil. Use std::fs::File (Rust opens with FILE_SHARE_READ|WRITE on Windows by default; add FILE_SHARE_DELETE via OpenOptionsExt::share_mode(7) so Claude can rename/delete). Paths on macOS use '/', so do not hardcode '\\'.

name: Incremental transcript reading + cache
description: Growing transcripts are re-read only from where the last read stopped, so live sessions update cheaply every 2 s.
behavior_details:
Cache 1: key = path + "|" + LastWriteTimeUtc ticks -> SessionInfo (unchanged file = instant hit). Cache 2 (ParseState per path, case-insensitive): Offset = byte offset after last complete '
'; Cwd/Prompt/Title/Summary/Count. On read: if file length < Offset (rewritten shorter) reset state to zero. Seek to Offset, read 1 MiB chunks, split on byte '
', decode UTF-8 per line (carry partial line across chunks). A trailing line without '
' is parsed into a COPY of the state for this result only, and re-read next time once complete. Per-file lock so parallel reads don't race. Errors -> return last state copy.
cross_platform_plan: Rust: HashMap<PathBuf, ParseState> behind Mutex (or DashMap) with per-entry Mutex; key on (path, mtime) for the SessionInfo cache. Use byte-level splitting (memchr) and String::from_utf8_lossy. Case-insensitive path keys only on Windows; on macOS (APFS default case-insensitive but preserving) normalise via the path as returned by read_dir.

name: Parallel warm-up and index build
description: At startup all transcripts of all profiles are parsed in the background so the UI shows quickly; then an in-memory index path->session is built and patched only for changed files.
behavior_details: WarmAsync: Parallel.For over all files, max degree = max(1, CPU count - 1), each worker thread at BelowNormal priority, exceptions ignored. WarmDone polled by a UI timer (ps1:847) then Complete-Warmup calls BuildIndex. BuildIndex: path -> SessionInfo for Count>0 only. Update-Index (ps1:176-187): for each changed path (from file watchers), remove from index, then if it matches `^(.*)\\projects\\[^\\]+\\[^\\]+\.jsonl$` and exists, re-read with account = capture group 1, add if Count>0; IndexVersion++ invalidates project caches.
data_sources: All <profile>/projects/*/*.jsonl across profiles from Get-Accounts (default ~/.claude, $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, and ~/.claude-* dirs containing projects, .credentials.json or settings.json).
cross_platform_plan: Rust: rayon par_iter (or std::thread::scope with N-1 threads) at startup in a tauri async command / spawn_blocking; emit an event when done. Use the notify crate for file watching (ReadDirectoryChangesW on Windows, FSEvents on macOS) and re-parse only changed paths. Path regex must accept both separators: use Path components (parent.parent file_name == "projects") instead of a regex. Lower thread priority is optional (std has none; can skip).

name: Folder grouping (Projects.Group) with pinned folders
description: Sessions are grouped by working folder; pinned folders appear first with a star icon even if they have no sessions; folders that no longer exist are shown dimmed with a 'missing' icon.
behavior_details: Filter by profile (case-insensitive equality on Account) unless profile empty (= all profiles). Group key = Cwd with trailing '\\' trimmed, else Slug (the encoded dir name) when Cwd unknown; key compare case-insensitive. Last = newest session Time. Pinned (settings.json `pinned` string array, trailing '\\' trimmed) creates empty entries if absent and sets Pinned=true. Missing = !Directory.Exists(path). Sessions sorted newest first. Folders sorted: pinned first, then Last desc. Result cached per key "profile|IndexVersion|pinned joined by ';'". CountFor(profile) = number of indexed sessions for that profile (profile card counts).
cross_platform_plan: Rust fn group(sessions, profile, pinned) -> Vec<Project>. Trim trailing '/' and '\\'. Case-insensitive key on Windows; on macOS compare case-sensitively or lowercase (APFS default is case-insensitive, lowercasing is acceptable). Existence check with Path::exists. Already partly in sessions.rs::projects(); add pinned + missing + sort rule.

name: Relative time text (Projects.Ago)
description: Short 'when' labels next to folders and sessions.
behavior_details: MinValue -> "no sessions"; <1 min -> "just now"; <60 min -> "{m}m ago"; <24 h -> "{floor h}h ago"; <2 days -> "Yesterday"; <7 days -> "{floor d}d ago"; else same year "MMM d" (e.g. "Oct 3"), other year "MMM d, yyyy". Uses local time.
cross_platform_plan: Implement in TS (frontend formats from epoch ms) so it refreshes without a backend call. Use Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US',{month:'short',day:'numeric'}).

name: Flat folder list rows with search (Projects.Rows)
description: Older flat list: one row per folder with 'N sessions · ago' subtitle, filtered by a search string.
behavior_details: Query matches if folder path contains query (case-insensitive) OR any session Label contains it. Title = last path segment (or full path if empty, e.g. drive root). Subtitle = "{n} session(s)   ·   {Ago(Last)}". Key = lower-case path. Dim + muted 'missing' icon when Missing; star icon when Pinned; else folder icon in accent color.
cross_platform_plan: Probably superseded by Tree.Build in the current UI; implement only if the flat view is kept. Filtering can live in TS.

name: Sidebar tree: PROJECTS groups + FOLDERS (Tree.Build)
description: Sidebar shows a PROJECTS section with user-made groups (each listing its folders) and a FOLDERS section with every folder not in a group. Groups collapse, long groups show 5 folders + 'Show N more', empty groups show 'Drag folders here'.
behavior_details: Inputs: groups from settings (names, folders[][], collapsed[], showAll per group (session-only, not persisted: $script:ShowAllFolders), foldersCollapsed). Rows: section 's:projects' "PROJECTS" (h30, not a drop target). Per group: folders = group's paths (trim '\\'), marked used; folder not in list -> placeholder ProjectInfo with Missing check. Group sessions = union of its folders' sessions sorted desc; Badge = total session count; Last = newest. Search: group shown if name matches or any folder matches; folder Matches = leaf name contains q OR any session (Label != "(no prompt)") Full contains q (case-insensitive). Group row key 'g:'+lower(name), kind group, h34, AcceptsDrop, chevron down when open. Open = searching || !collapsed. When open: show all if searching, showAll, or <=6 folders; else first 5 then 'more' row "Show {n} more" (key 'm:'+lower name, h28, indent 1); if expanded and >6 (not searching) add "Show less". Zero folders -> hint "Drag folders here". No groups shown -> hint "No matching projects" (searching) or "No projects yet. Click + to create one.". Folder rows: key 'f:'+lower(path), kind folder, h32, indent 1 in group / 0 in FOLDERS, Draggable, Detail = Ago(Last) only if it has sessions. FOLDERS section 's:folders' title "FOLDERS  ·  {count}", AcceptsDrop (dropping a folder there removes it from its group), chevron; open when searching or !foldersCollapsed. A folder can be in a group AND is then excluded from FOLDERS.
data_sources: settings.json group list (name, folders, collapsed) and folders-collapsed flag — exact key names live in ClaudeManager.ps1 (other slice; see ps1:773).
cross_platform_plan: Build tree rows in TS from backend Project list + settings (pure data transform; fast). Drag-and-drop with HTML5 DnD or pointer events in the webview. Keep identical row keys/heights so selection survives refresh.

name: Local token usage accounting (Usage.Compute)
description: Counts tokens Claude Code recorded in transcripts on this PC: today, last 7 days (bar sparkline), and the current 5-hour window. Nothing is sent anywhere.
behavior_details: Roots = <profile>/projects for the profile in view (all profiles when viewing all). Enumerate *.jsonl RECURSIVELY (includes subagent transcripts), skip files with mtime older than now-8 days. Per file (cached by full path + mtime ticks): read every line; prefilter: line contains `"usage"` and `"assistant"`; JSON: root.type == "assistant"; message.usage exists; skip if message.model == "<synthetic>"; root.timestamp string parsed as UTC (ISO) -> local. Tokens = input_tokens + output_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens (cache_read_input_tokens deliberately EXCLUDED). Id = message.id. Aggregate: drop entries older than 8 days; dedupe by message.id across all files (a reply is logged once per content block; null ids never deduped). Sort by time. 5-hour blocks: new block when none yet, or t >= start+5h, or gap since previous entry >= 5h; block start = entry time floored to the hour (local). PeakBlock = max tokens of any block (incl. current). Days[0..6], index 6 = today: day = 6 - (today - entryDate in days); Week = sum over those 7 days. Today/TodayReplies for today's date. Current block active if now < start+5h -> BlockStart, BlockTokens, BlockReplies. Fraction = BlockTokens/PeakBlock clamped to 1 (0 if inactive). ResetsAt = BlockStart+5h. Runs on a background thread (BelowNormal), only one at a time (busyLocal guard; the latest roots are remembered but a concurrent call is dropped).
cross_platform_plan: Rust command usage_local(roots) run in spawn_blocking; walkdir recursive; cache HashMap<path,(mtime,Vec<Entry>)>; serde_json::Value per filtered line; chrono for local-time flooring and dates. Return the report struct to TS. Identical on both OSes.

name: Number and countdown formatting (Usage.Fmt / Until / Plan.ResetText)
description: Compact token numbers and 'resets in' text.
behavior_details: Fmt: >=1,000,000 -> M with 1 decimal (no decimal when >=10M), e.g. 1.2M, 12M; >=1000 -> K with 1 decimal (none when >=100K); else integer. Until(t): <1 min -> "less than a minute"; >=1h -> "{h}h {m}m"; else "{m}m {ss}s". ResetText(t): null -> ""; when = "h:mm tt" if today, "tomorrow h:mm tt" if tomorrow, else "ddd h:mm tt"; <1 min left -> "Resets now"; <24 h -> "Resets in {Until}  ·  {when}"; else "Resets {when}". Level color: >=90% danger red, >=70% orange #FF9F0A, else accent.
cross_platform_plan: Pure TS helpers; re-render every 30 s (the panel's clock timer) so countdowns stay current.

name: Plan limits from Anthropic OAuth usage API (Plan.Fetch)
description: Shows the same numbers as Claude Code's /usage: 'Current session' and 'Weekly · <model>' percentages with reset times, per signed-in profile.
behavior_details: Credentials: <profile>/.credentials.json -> claudeAiOauth.accessToken (string), .expiresAt (epoch ms number), .subscriptionType (plan name, e.g. "max"/"pro"). Errors: file missing or no token -> "Not signed in"; expiresAt>0 and in the past -> "Sign-in expired — use this profile once to refresh" (app never refreshes tokens itself). Request: GET https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage, headers `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, `anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20`, `User-Agent: claude-manager`; HTTP timeout 15 s. 429: wait = Retry-After delta seconds or 120 if absent, clamped to [600, 3600] s; global (all profiles) retryAfter = now+wait; error "Usage service busy". 401 -> sign-in expired text; other non-2xx -> "Usage service unavailable ({code})". Network/aggregate exception -> "Could not reach Anthropic (offline?)"; other -> "Could not read usage". Parse new shape: root.limits[] each {kind, group, scope.model.display_name, percent, resets_at}; Label = group=="session" ? "Current session" : group=="weekly" ? "Weekly · " + (model ?? "all models") : kind with '_'->' '. Percent number; resets_at ISO -> local. Fallback (no limits[]): keys five_hour -> "Current session", seven_day -> "Weekly · all models", each {utilization, resets_at}. Throttle: per-credentials-path memo of last SUCCESSFUL report reused if <5 min old (comment says 45 s, code is 5 min); during retryAfter return "Usage service busy" without calling. Source field "api" ('status' = Claude status line is declared but never produced in this code). Token is never written anywhere.
cross_platform_plan: Rust with reqwest (rustls) in a tauri async command; keep the token in Rust only, never send it to the webview. macOS: Claude Code stores OAuth credentials in the login Keychain (generic password, service "Claude Code-credentials", account = $USER; value is the same JSON with claudeAiOauth) rather than .credentials.json — read it with the security-framework crate (or `security find-generic-password -s "Claude Code-credentials" -w`), falling back to .credentials.json. For non-default profiles (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) on macOS the Keychain service name gets a suffix derived from the config dir hash; verify empirically and fall back to the file. Treat 'signed in' check (ps1 Test-Path .credentials.json) the same way on macOS.

name: Plan-limit disk cache (usage-cache.json)
description: Last good plan percentages are saved so the usage popover is never empty at startup.
behavior_details: Path = <SettingsDir>/usage-cache.json (SettingsDir = %APPDATA%\ClaudeManager). Saved after every plan refresh: JSON array of {profile, plan, fetched (ISO 8601 round-trip 'o'), limits:[{label, percent, resets (ISO or null)}]}; reports with no limits are skipped. NEVER contains tokens. Load(names): only entries whose profile is in names; used when nothing is shown yet or the profile set changed. All errors swallowed.
cross_platform_plan: Store in Tauri app_data_dir (Windows %APPDATA%\<bundle id>, macOS ~/Library/Application Support/<bundle id>); keep same JSON shape; optionally migrate from %APPDATA%\ClaudeManager on first run on Windows.

name: Plan refresh orchestration, stale handling and self-heal
description: Plans refresh in the background while the old numbers stay visible; transient failures keep showing the last good numbers marked as stale.
behavior_details: ReloadPlans(creds[], names[]): if nothing shown or profiles changed, show cached numbers immediately. Skip network if a refresh is running, or if same profiles AND fetched <300 s ago AND every report has limits or is 'Not signed in'. Fetch sequentially per profile on a background thread. Merge: if new result has a transient error (not starting with "Sign-in" or "Not signed") and old result for that profile had limits, keep old with Stale = error; else take new. Save cache, update ring. PlansNeedRetry = no plans OR any plan without limits whose error isn't "Not signed..."; on window activation (form Activated, app loaded, picker hidden) retry if needed. PlansStale(sec) compares Plans[0].FetchedAt. SessionPercent = max 'Current session' percent across shown profiles, -1 if none. Profiles in scope: the open profile, or all profiles with credentials when 'All profiles'.
cross_platform_plan: Rust owns the throttle/memo state (Mutex<HashMap>), TS owns display state. Trigger refresh on window focus (Tauri WindowEvent::Focused(true)) and on the periodic timer from the ps1 (LastPlanRefresh, other slice). Emit 'usage-updated' events.

name: Usage popover content (UsagePanel)
description: Popover: 'USAGE' header with scope and plan name, a status line, per-limit bars with % and reset text, and a footer with this PC's today/week tokens plus a 7-day mini bar chart.
behavior_details: Header right: Scope (profile name or 'All profiles'); when exactly one plan with a plan name, "{scope}  ·  {Capitalized plan} plan"; spinner while loading. Status line: no plans -> "Loading your plan limits..." (busy) / "Plan limits not loaded yet"; any stale -> "Numbers from {ago}  ·  usage service busy, will check again shortly"; no successful fetch -> "Checking..." / "No plan limits available"; else "Updated {ago}" + "  ·  refreshing..." when busy. ago: <5 s "just now", <60 s "{s}s ago", <60 min "{m}m ago", else "h:mm tt". Multiple profiles -> bold profile name heading per profile. Error -> muted error text only. Limit row (52 px): label left, "{round(%)}% used" right in level color, 6 px rounded track with fill (min width = track height), reset text below. No plans yet -> 2 breathing skeleton rows. Footer: separator, "This PC: counting..." or "This PC  ·  today {Fmt}  ·  week {Fmt}", 7 bars (60 px wide, 18 px tall, scaled to max day, min 2 px, today accent, others muted 45%). Redraw every 30 s; popover resizes to content (ContentChanged).
cross_platform_plan: HTML/CSS popover in the webview anchored to the title-bar ring; CSS transitions for bars; shimmer skeleton via CSS animation. UI details belong to the UI slice; data contract described here.

name: Title-bar usage ring (UsageRing)
description: Small ring in the title bar showing the highest current-session % (or local block fraction if no plan data); hovering/clicking opens the usage popover.
behavior_details: State 0 loading: spinning 70° arc (9°/30 ms). State 1: arc from 12 o'clock, 360*fraction, spring-animated (response 0.6, damping 1), color by level. State 2 (plans present but none has limits): muted ring with a 40° red arc at top. Fraction = SessionPercent/100 if >=0 else local Report.Fraction. Popover opens immediately on mouse enter and on click; 120 ms poll closes it once the cursor is over neither ring nor popover.
cross_platform_plan: SVG circle with stroke-dasharray in TS; spring from src/spring.ts. Hover-intent close via pointerleave on both ring and popover with a short delay. On macOS with native traffic lights (titleBarStyle overlay) leave space on the left.

name: Git command runner (Git.Run / RunTagged)
description: All source-control features run the git CLI in the background and deliver (exit code, stdout, stderr) back to the UI.
behavior_details: Process 'git' with args string, WorkingDirectory = repo dir, no window, stdout/stderr UTF-8 captured concurrently, optional stdin text (then stdin closed). Env: GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 (never hang on credential prompt), LANG=en_US.UTF-8 (English output for parsing). Exception -> code -1, error = message. Callback ignored if the UI is disposed. RunTagged passes a caller tag back so stale responses (user switched folder) can be dropped. History query used by the app: `log --branches --remotes --tags HEAD --date-order -n 400 --pretty=format:%H%x1f%P%x1f%s%x1f%an%x1f%ar%x1f%D%x1e` (records split by 0x1E, fields by 0x1F; HEAD detection regex `(^|, )HEAD($| ->|,)` on %D; ref pills: drop 'HEAD' and '*/HEAD', 'HEAD -> x' becomes '*x', strip 'tag: '; relative date shortened: ' ago' removed, seconds->s, minutes->m, hours->h, days->d, weeks->w, months->mo, years->y, ', '->' ').
cross_platform_plan: Rust tauri command git(dir, args: Vec<String>, stdin: Option<String>) -> {code, stdout, stderr} via std::process::Command (pass args as a Vec, not a single string, to avoid quoting bugs). On Windows set CREATION_FLAGS CREATE_NO_WINDOW (0x08000000). On macOS GUI apps get a minimal PATH: resolve git from /usr/bin/git, /opt/homebrew/bin, /usr/local/bin or the login shell PATH (e.g. fix-path-env crate). Request ids in TS replace RunTagged tags.

name: Commit graph lane layout (GitGraph.Layout)
description: History list draws a colored branch/merge graph beside each commit, VS Code style.
behavior_details: Input newest-first: hashes[], parents[] (space-separated %P), heads[] (HEAD commit). lanes = list of awaited hash or null; colors parallel; nextColor counter; MaxLanes starts 1. Per commit c: lane = index of c in lanes; if absent take first null lane or append, and assign colors[lane]=nextColor++. Row.Lane, Row.Color = colors[lane], Merge = parents>1, Head. Top half segments: for each non-null lane k: if lanes[k]==c segment (k,0)->(lane,1) color colors[k], else straight (k,0)->(k,2). Then set all lanes==c to null. Bottom half if parents: j = index of parent0; if j>=0 and j!=lane -> seg (lane,1)->(j,2) color colors[j] (lane stays freed); else lanes[lane]=parent0, colors[lane]=row color, seg (lane,1)->(lane,2). For each other parent p: t = its lane, else first null or append with new color nextColor++, lanes[t]=p; seg (lane,1)->(t,2) color colors[t]. Trim trailing null lanes. Row.Lanes = max(max x of segs + 1, lane+1); MaxLanes = max. Y coords: 0 top, 1 dot (middle), 2 bottom. The UI caps drawn lanes at min(8, MaxLanes). Colors are palette indexes (mod palette size).
cross_platform_plan: Port 1:1 to TS (pure function, cheap for 400 commits) or Rust; draw per row with a small inline SVG/canvas. Keep the exact algorithm so the graph looks the same.

name: Change list data model (ChangeItem)
description: Data shape for the STAGED CHANGES / CHANGES list.
behavior_details: ChangeItem: Kind 'file'|'section', Section 'staged'|'changes', Path, Name, Dir, Status (status letter), Count (for section headers). Actions are raised as (Item, Action string). Parsing of git status into items is in ClaudeManager.ps1 (other slice); rendering in ChangeList (UI slice).
cross_platform_plan: Define a TS type; parse `git status --porcelain=v1 -z` in Rust for robustness with spaces/unicode paths.

name: Live / working session detection (LiveScan.Scan)
description: Marks sessions that are running ('Open now') or actively working ('Working...'), and folders containing them; feeds notifications and tray toasts.
behavior_details: For each profile dir: (A) <profile>/sessions/*.json: JSON {pid:number, sessionId:string, status?:string, cwd?:string}; skip if no pid or sessionId. Check process: if not found / exited -> DELETE the json file and skip. If alive but process name (lower, no .exe) not in {claude, node, pwsh, powershell, cmd, bash, wt, windowsterminal, conhost, openconsole} -> PID reused, skip but keep the file. Level = 2 if status=="busy" else 1. (B) Newer Claude Code writes <profile>/sessions/<pid>.<hash>.key (no session id): parse pid = text before first '.', skip if already listed or process dead; collect (pid, process StartTime); sort by start time ascending (so older processes claim files first). For each: id = session UUID from the process command line via regex `(?:--resume|-r|--session-id)[ =]+"?([0-9a-fA-F]{8}-...-[0-9a-fA-F]{12})`; if found locate <profile>/projects/*/<id>.jsonl; else NewestSince: newest *.jsonl in projects/*/ with mtime > processStart-5 s not already taken. Skip if none or id already listed. Cwd = LastCwd(jsonl): read last 256 KiB, regex `"cwd":"((?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)"`, take last match, JSON-unescape. Level = 2 if jsonl mtime < 8 s ago else 1. Command line read via NtQueryInformationProcess class 60 (ProcessCommandLineInformation) with PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION, cached per pid (cache cleared when >500 entries). Caller (ps1 Update-Live, every 2 s timer): dedupe same SessionId preferring the one reachable from a window, else higher Level; LiveCwd map lower(cwd trimmed)->max level; change signature 'id=level;...' sorted triggers UI refresh.
data_sources: <profile>/sessions/*.json, <profile>/sessions/*.key, <profile>/projects/*/*.jsonl, OS process table (name, start time, command line)
cross_platform_plan: Rust with the sysinfo crate: Process::name, start_time, cmd() (works on Windows and macOS without NtQueryInformationProcess; on macOS uses KERN_PROCARGS2, same-user processes only, which is fine). Allowed process names on macOS: add 'zsh', 'sh', 'fish', 'login', 'Terminal', 'iTerm2', and the Tauri app itself (claude runs under our pty shell); compare names with .exe stripped and lowercase. On macOS the node-based claude may show name 'node' or 'claude' — both allowed. Run on a 2 s interval in a background task, diff the signature and emit 'live-changed' only on change. Deleting stale json is a write into the user's Claude dir — keep it (matches current behavior). Reachability check (window handle) is Windows-only in ps1; in Tauri prefer sessions whose pid belongs to one of our own pty children, else higher level.

name: Find child process by exe name (Native.FindChild)
description: Finds the pwsh.exe child of a launched process (to locate the console window of a new terminal).
behavior_details: Toolhelp32 snapshot (TH32CS_SNAPPROCESS=2), returns first process with ParentProcessID==parent and exe name equal (case-insensitive), else 0. ~1 ms vs ~75 ms for WMI.
cross_platform_plan: Not needed: Tauri spawns shells directly via portable-pty and knows the child pid. If parent/child lookup is needed (e.g. killing orphan claude + parent shell), use sysinfo Process::parent() on both OSes.

name: Console window embedding (Native.FindConsoleWindow / Embed / Unembed / UnembedHidden / FindWindowThread / MoveWindow / PostMessage WM_CLOSE)
description: Current Windows app runs each Claude session in a real conhost console window and reparents it into the app as a borderless child; it can pop it out to a normal window, hide it to keep it running in the background, or close it.
behavior_details: FindConsoleWindow(pid): EnumWindows for a window owned by pid with class 'ConsoleWindowClass'. Embed: strip WS_CAPTION|WS_THICKFRAME|WS_MINIMIZEBOX|WS_MAXIMIZEBOX|WS_SYSMENU|WS_POPUP, add WS_CHILD|WS_VISIBLE, SetParent, SWP frame change, show; returns old style. UnembedHidden: SetParent(null), remove WS_VISIBLE, SWP_HIDEWINDOW (session keeps running hidden). Unembed: restore style + visible, position (form.Left+60, form.Top+60, 1100x680 scaled), bring to front. FindWindowThread: finds the conhost thread that owns the hwnd (GetWindowThreadProcessId reports the shell thread) for AttachThreadInput focus forwarding. Close = PostMessage WM_CLOSE (0x10). GetTitle reads the console title to derive the chat name.
cross_platform_plan: Drop entirely: Tauri uses xterm.js over portable-pty (ConPTY on Windows, openpty on macOS). Equivalents: 'pop out' = open the terminal in a new Tauri WebviewWindow attached to the same pty; 'keep running in background' = keep the pty alive with the tab hidden; close = kill pty child; chat name = OSC 0/2 title sequences via xterm.js onTitleChange.

name: Bring window to front (Native.BringToFront)
description: Focus the app (or an external terminal running a session) when a toast is clicked or a live session is opened.
behavior_details: If not visible ShowWindow(SW_SHOW=5); if minimized ShowWindow(SW_RESTORE=9); SetForegroundWindow. Used for the main form from tray balloon / double-click, and for external console or Windows Terminal windows hosting a session (walk claude -> shell -> host up to 6 levels).
cross_platform_plan: For our own window: Tauri window.unminimize(); show(); set_focus() (works on both OSes; on macOS also app.show() / NSApp activate). Focusing external terminals not started by us: Windows via the windows crate (SetForegroundWindow + AllowSetForegroundWindow); macOS via `osascript -e 'tell application "Terminal" to activate'` / NSRunningApplication.activate by pid of the ancestor app — best-effort, can be dropped in favor of resuming inside the app.

name: Dark title bar / dark mode Win32 hooks (DwmSetWindowAttribute, SetWindowTheme, SetPreferredAppMode, AllowDarkModeForWindow, RefreshImmersiveColorPolicyState)
description: Makes native menus, scrollbars and the window frame dark when the OS is in dark mode.
behavior_details: SetPreferredAppMode(2 = ForceDark) + RefreshImmersiveColorPolicyState when $Dark; DWM attribute (immersive dark mode, attr 20) on windows; SetWindowTheme('DarkMode_Explorer') on controls.
cross_platform_plan: Tauri: set window theme to follow system (theme: null) and use CSS prefers-color-scheme; custom frameless title bar (decorations:false on Windows, titleBarStyle:'Overlay' + hiddenTitle on macOS for native traffic lights). Listen to tauri://theme-changed. No Win32 calls needed.

name: Timer resolution and GDI blitting helpers (timeBeginPeriod, BitBlt, AlphaBlend, CreateCompatibleDC)
description: Used for smooth 60 fps spring animations and window fade effects in WinForms.
behavior_details: timeBeginPeriod(1) for 1 ms timers; GDI helpers for fade overlay snapshots; ReleaseCapture/SendMessage for dragging the borderless window.
cross_platform_plan: Drop: use requestAnimationFrame + src/spring.ts in the webview; window dragging via data-tauri-drag-region / startDragging().
